newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: S&P affirms National Foods rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms National Foods rating.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Tuesday that it affirmed the BBB corporate credit rating on National Foods Ltd.
The ratings agency said the rating outlook had been revised to negative from stable.
S&P said the affirmation followed National Foods sale on February 5 of its consumer goods unit NationalPak to First Brands Corp.

"Despite short-term debt reduction and improvement in cash flow protection measures, the A$206 million sale of NFL's most profitable unit, and the resulting focus on more competitive, lower margin dairy and fruit juice businesses, have weakened the group's overall businesses," it said.
"Standard and Poor's will assess NFL's ongoing growth strategy of reinvestment into the existing businesses."
"Maintenance of the current rating is dependent on obtaining improvements in margin and cash flow generation in core units.
"However, unsuccessful reinvestment of the NationalPak sales proceeds, and consequent inability to achieve these improvements, could lead to pressure on the existing rating," S&P said.
The ratings agency said NationalPak was National Foods' best-performing unit, representing about 33 percent of earnings before interest and tax and about 23 percent of total assets.
National Foods said it sold the unit for a profit of about A$70 million.
